meta.name: Send weekly client re-engagement emails with Gmail, Google Sheets, and Slack

name: Weekly Client Engagement Automation with GoHighLevel, Gmail, Slack, and Sheets1

parameters.content:
## 📋 Weekly Client Engagement Pulse

This workflow automatically identifies clients who haven't been contacted in 14+ days and sends:
- ✉️ Re-engagement email to inactive clients
- 📊 Google Sheets log for tracking
- 💬 Slack notification to account managers

**Runs:** Every Monday at 9:00 AM

**What it does:**
1. Reads all contact rows from Google Sheets (Sheet1)
2. Filters contacts inactive for 14+ days (by `Last Activity Date`)
3. Sends a re-engagement email per inactive contact
4. Appends each one to a Google Sheets log (Sheet2)
5. Posts a Slack summary (top 10) to the team
6. Catches errors and alerts Slack

**Setup Time:** ~10 minutes

---

### 🎯 Use Case
Perfect for agencies, consultants, and service businesses who need to maintain regular client touchpoints and prevent churn.

### ⚠️ Known Issues in Current Setup
- Re-engagement email "To" field is hardcoded, not the contact's own address
- Email body uses `{{ $json.firstName }}`, but the real field is `First Name` — greeting always falls back to "there"
- Append row step has no matching column, so reruns can create duplicate log rows
- Slack summary lists at most 10 names even if more contacts are inactive

## ⏰ Schedule Trigger Node

**What it does:**
Automatically runs this workflow every Monday at 9:00 AM.

**Cron Expression:** `0 9 * * 1`
- `0` = Minute (0)
- `9` = Hour (9 AM)
- `*` = Any day of month
- `*` = Any month
- `1` = Monday (0=Sunday, 1=Monday)

**Customization Examples:**
- Daily at 9 AM: `0 9 * * *`
- Every 4 hours: `0 */4 * * *`
- Weekdays at 2 PM: `0 14 * * 1-5`

**Testing:**
Click "Test workflow" button to run manually before enabling schedule.

## 📊 Google Sheets Read Node

**Node name:** Get row(s) in sheet

**What it does:**
Reads ALL rows from the source Google Sheet.

**Setup Steps:**4. Select spreadsheet: **Client Engagement Automation**
5. Select sheet: **Sheet1**

**Operation:** Get Row(s) — no filters

**Expected Columns in Sheet1:**
- First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone
- Company, Last Activity Date

**Output:**
One item per row, plus an auto-added `row_number` field.

**Note:** No filtering happens here — filtering happens in the next node, based on `Last Activity Date`.

## 🔍 Filter Inactive Contacts

**Node name:** Filter Inactive Contacts (14+ days)

**What it does:**
Identifies contacts with NO activity in the last 14 days.

**Logic:**
```javascript
const fourteenDaysAgo = new Date();
fourteenDaysAgo.setDate(fourteenDaysAgo.getDate() - 14);

const lastActivityDate = new Date(item.json["Last Activity Date"]);

if (lastActivityDate < fourteenDaysAgo) {
  // push to inactiveContacts with daysSinceContact + needsAttention
}
```

**Uses This Field:**
- `Last Activity Date` (from the sheet, e.g. "4/15/2026")

**Adds:**
- `daysSinceContact` = calculated days since last activity
- `needsAttention` = true flag

**Output Shape:**
Returns a SINGLE item: `{ json: { inactiveContacts: [...] } }` — the array is unpacked by the next node (Split Out).

**Customize:** Change `14` to any number of days.

## 📤 Split Out Node

**Node name:** Split Out

**What it does:**
Unpacks the `inactiveContacts` array (from the previous Code node) into individual items, one per contact.

**Why needed:**
The filter node returns one item holding an array. Downstream nodes (email, sheet logging) need one item per contact.

**Field Split Out:** `inactiveContacts`

**Fields on Each Resulting Item:**
- row_number, First Name, Last Name
- Email, Phone, Company
- Last Activity Date, daysSinceContact, needsAttention

**Example:**
1 item with 23 inactive contacts → 23 separate items flowing through the workflow.

## ❓ IF Condition Node

**Node name:** IF: Needs Attention

**What it does:**
Double-checks that each contact truly needs attention before acting.

**Condition:**
```
needsAttention === true
```

**True Branch (only branch wired):**
Runs two paths in parallel:
- Send Re-engagement Email
- Append row in sheet → Format Slack Message → Send Slack Notification

**False Branch:**
Not connected — non-matching items are simply dropped.

**Best Practice:**
Always validate critical flags before taking action like sending emails.

## 📧 Gmail Send Email Node

**Node name:** Send Re-engagement Email

**What it does:**
Sends a re-engagement email for each inactive contact.

**Current Setup:**
- **To:** hardcoded to `data.saurabh099@gmail.com` ⚠️ — not the contact's own email. Replace with `={{ $json.Email }}` to send to each contact individually.
- **Subject:** "Just Checking In!"

**⚠️ Personalization Bug:**
The HTML body uses `{{ $json.firstName || 'there' }}`, but the actual field from the sheet is `First Name` (capitalized, with a space). Since `firstName` doesn't exist, every email greets the contact as "there". Fix by changing the expression to `{{ $json['First Name'] || 'there' }}`.

**Email Template:**
Professional HTML with a gradient header, greeting, short copy, and a "Get in Touch" button linking to `mailto:support@yourcompany.com`.

**Customize:**
- Fix the `To` field and `firstName` reference above
- Update colors, branding, copy, and support email

## 📊 Google Sheets Log Node

**Node name:** Append row in sheet

**What it does:**
Appends each inactive contact to a log sheet in the same spreadsheet used for the source data.

**Current Setup:**
- **Spreadsheet:** Client Engagement Automation
- **Sheet:** Sheet2 (separate tab from the Sheet1 source data)
- **Operation:** Append

**Columns Mapped:**
- First Name, Last Name, Email
- Phone, Company, Last Activity Date

**⚠️ No Matching Column Set:**
`matchingColumns` is empty, so nothing prevents duplicate rows — re-running the workflow on the same inactive contact will append it again. Consider setting Email (or row_number) as a matching column.

**Purpose:**
- Audit trail of all re-engagement attempts
- Feeds directly into the Slack summary (next node)

## 🔄 Format Slack Message

**Node name:** Format Slack Message

**What it does:**
Aggregates inactive contacts that were just logged and builds a Slack summary.

**Processing:**
1. Maps every input item to `{ name, company, days }`
2. Recalculates `days` from `Last Activity Date` (independent of `daysSinceContact`)
3. Takes only the **first 10** contacts for the message body
4. Joins them into a bulleted list

**Output Format:**
```
🚨 Weekly Client Engagement Pulse

23 clients need attention (no contact in 14+ days):

• Vikas Verma | SmartBiz | 69 days since last contact
• Sneha Yadav | DataWorks | 30 days since last contact
...
```

**Variables Created:**
- `count` = TOTAL number of inactive clients (not capped)
- `clientList` = formatted bullet list, capped at 10 entries

**⚠️ Note:** No `clients` array or email addresses are included in the output — only name, company, and days.

**Customization:**
Edit the JavaScript to raise/remove the 10-client cap or add fields like email.

## 💬 Slack Notification Node

**Node name:** Send Slack Notification to Account Manager

**What it does:**
Posts the weekly summary to the team.

**Current Setup:**
- **Channel:** #all-client-automation-lab
- **Markdown Enabled:** Yes

**Message Includes:**
- 🚨 Alert header
- Total count of inactive clients (`{{ $json.count }}`)
- Bulleted list (`{{ $json.clientList }}`) — name, company, and days since contact for up to 10 clients
- Call to action to follow up

**Note:** Email addresses are NOT included in this message (see Format Slack Message note).

**Best Practice:**
If you want a dedicated channel instead of reusing #all-client-automation-lab, create one like `#client-engagement`.

## 🚨 Error Trigger Node

**What it does:**
Automatically catches ANY error in this workflow.

**Triggers When:**
- API connection fails
- Authentication expires
- Rate limits hit
- Invalid data format
- Network timeouts
- Any node throws error

**Captures:**
- `node.name` = which node failed
- `error.message` = error description
- `timestamp` = when it happened
- Full error stack trace

**Why Critical:**
Without this, workflow fails silently and you don't know:
- Emails weren't sent
- Clients weren't tracked
- System is broken

**Best Practice:**
ALWAYS include error handling in production workflows.

## 📢 Error Alert to Slack

**Node name:** Send Error Alert to Slack

**What it does:**
Notifies the team when any node in this workflow throws an error.

**Current Setup:**
- **Channel:** #all-client-automation-lab (same channel as the weekly summary — not a separate error channel)

**Actual Message Format:**
```
🚨 n8n Workflow Failed

📌 Workflow: {{ $json.workflow.name }}

🔴 Failed Node:
{{ $json.execution.lastNodeExecuted }}

❌ Error:
{{ $json.execution.error.message }}

🔗 Execution:
{{ $json.execution.url }}

🆘 Execution ID:
{{ $json.execution.id }}
Please investigate immediately.
```

**Pro Tip:**
Consider routing this to a dedicated `#errors` or `#n8n-monitoring` channel so critical failures don't get lost in the regular weekly summary thread.
